subject.title: fix (Computer Use) Stabilize Codex Computer Use readiness

question: Should OpenClaw accept this Codex Computer Use readiness hardening as the default path, including fail-closed live `list_apps` probes, shared per-agent cache reconciliation, and the narrow sandbox-guard exception for the readiness probe?
rationale: The patch appears technically coherent, but it changes startup/readiness defaults, native MCP probing, and process/availability behavior in a bundled Codex integration where repository policy requires owner acceptance beyond green CI.

options.title: Accept After Docs Fix
options.body: Fix the opt-in repair wording and then accept the compatibility, security-boundary, and availability tradeoffs as the intended Computer Use readiness contract.

options.title: Narrow Defaults Further
options.body: Keep the live status command but make stricter startup fail-closed behavior or shared cache reconciliation opt-in until more upgrade proof exists.

options.title: Pause For Codex API Shape
options.body: Hold the PR until Codex exposes a stronger first-party readiness or cache-refresh API that avoids OpenClaw-owned cache reconciliation and direct MCP probing.

recommendation.title: Accept After Docs Fix
recommendation.body: Fix the opt-in repair wording and then accept the compatibility, security-boundary, and availability tradeoffs as the intended Computer Use readiness contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current Computer Use setup boundary that this PR extends, so they are the best available routing signal for accepting or narrowing the integration contract.
